rationale: Evidence: all 60 development trials across oval, s-bend and slalom ended off track with zero completions. Progress stayed at 0.04 to 0.17, and max_error sat near 0.06 to 0.07, which is the off-track limit, so the robot drifts off the line early rather than slowly. Iteration 8 (score 40.4) was the best, with low speed (0.6), kp 1.2 and kd 0.6. Iteration 7 (kd 1.0, kp 1.6, base 0.9) gave a big slalom gain (46.1 vs 24.6) but lost oval score (47 vs 67). That suggests higher kd and kp help on tight bends, while lower speed helps the oval and s-bend. Steering oscillation is high in every run, so damping matters. The change: keep the iteration 8 geometry (proven, the outer sensors at +/-0.03 with 12 mm footprints, 0.4 kg, 0.14 m track, 0.03 m wheels), and move the controller toward the damped middle: kp 1.6, ki 0.3, kd 1.0, base_speed 0.7 (between the 0.6 and 0.9 runs). I expect slalom to keep most of its gain, oval to hold near the 40 to 60 range, and the overall score to land around 38 to 45. Sensor layout is unchanged so the comparison isolates the controller effect.
